'''Maciej Gliwicz''' ({{IPA|pl|ma.t͡ɕɛj glivit͡ʂ}}; born '''Zbigniew Maciej Gliwicz'''; 21 February 1939 – 2 June 2024) was a Polish biologist, [[evolutionism|evolutionist]] and professor at the [[University of Warsaw]] who specialised in the field of [[hydrobiology]].

==Life and scientific career==
Gliwicz graduated from the Faculty of Biology and Earth Sciences at the University of Warsaw in 1962. He obtained his [[doctoral degree]] in 1969 and became a [[Professor]] of Natural Sciences in 1988. Between 1987 and 1990 he worked as Deputy Dean of the Faculty of Biology at the University of Warsaw. Since the mid-1980 until 2009, he also worked as head of the Department of Hydrobiology at his alma mater. He collaborated with a number of international institutions including the [[Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology]] in [[Plön]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.biol.uw.edu.pl/pl/index.php?option=com_workforce&view=employee&id=252&Itemid=327 |title=Maciej Gliwicz prof. dr hab. emerytowny  |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Z_Gliwicz |title=Z. Maciej Gliwicz |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://diatoms.org/genera/gliwiczia |title=Gliwiczia |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref>

Gliwicz was an author and co-author of several hundred scientific papers and publications primarily in the field of hydrobiology with a special focus on [[behavioral ecology]]. Some of his interests concern predator-prey relations and [[trophic cascade]]s among [[aquatic organism]]s. He discovered the relationship between the size of filtrator and minimum quantity of threshold food, thus explaining some of the mechanisms of ecological competition and supporting the size-efficiency hypothesis.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Food thresholds and body size in cladocerans |journal=Nature |volume=343 |issue=6259 |pages=638–640 |bibcode=1990Natur.343..638G |last1=Gliwicz |first1=Z. Maciej |year=1990 |doi=10.1038/343638a0 |s2cid=4329614 }}</ref> He also described the phenomenon of the so-called "lunar trap" and explained the convergence of periodic population declines of [[zooplankton]] in African water reservoirs along the [[Zambezi]] and the [[lunar cycle]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |title=A Lunar Cycle in Zooplankton |journal = Ecology|volume = 67|issue = 4|pages = 883–897|jstor = 1939811|last1 = Gliwicz|first1 = Z. Maciej|year = 1986|doi = 10.2307/1939811| bibcode=1986Ecol...67..883G }}</ref>

Gliwicz was one of the members of [[limnologist]]s who were part of the Plankton Ecology Group, which devised the model of seasonal succession of planktonic events, accepted as the PEG standard model since mid-1980s.<ref>{{cite book | surname= Lampert W. | title= Ekologia wód śródlądowych | url = | date = 2001 | publisher= Wydawnictwo Naukowe PWN | place= Warszawa | isbn = 83-01-13387-2}}</ref> He also conducted research into the predation and the evolution of vertical migration in zooplankton.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Predation and the evolution of vertical migration in zooplankton |journal=Nature |volume=320 |issue=6064 |pages=746–748 |bibcode=1986Natur.320..746G |last1=Gliwicz |first1=Maciej Z. |year=1986 |doi=10.1038/320746a0 |s2cid=4318264 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/31982533 |title=Predation and the evolution of vertical migration in Zooplankton |journal=Nature |volume=320 |issue=6064 |pages=746–748 |access-date=6 July 2019|bibcode=1986Natur.320..746G |last1=Gliwicz |first1=Maciej Z. |year=1986 |doi=10.1038/320746a0 |s2cid=4318264 }}</ref>

In 2001, he won Poland's top scientific award, [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] in the category of [[life sciences]], for "revealing the role of predation in shaping animal demography, life histories and behaviour."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fnp.org.pl/prof-zbigniew-maciej-gliwicz/ |title=Prof. Zbigniew Maciej Gliwicz |access-date=5 July 2019}}</ref>

In 2012, he became the recipient (together with Winfried Lampert) of the [[A.C. Redfield Lifetime Achievement Award]] conferred by the [[American Society of Limnology and Oceanography]] "for their outstanding individual and collaborative research, which has laid the foundations for our current understanding of [[phytoplankton]]-zooplankton interactions, trophic ecology of zooplankton, and evolutionary relationships in [[freshwater]] [[ecosystem]]s."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pth.home.pl/pobierz/Wiadomosci_3_2012.pdf |title=Wiadomości Hydrobiologiczne |access-date=5 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325276230 |title=A.C. REDFIELD LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD TO Z. MACIEJ GLIWICZ AND WINFRIED LAMPERT |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref>

As a populariser of [[Neo-Darwinism]], he coorganized [[evolutionary biology]] workshops and he was appointed a supervisor of the University of Warsaw's [[honorary doctorate]] for American evolutionary geneticist [[Francisco J. Ayala]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uw.edu.pl/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/prof.francisco_j._ayala_publikacja_dhc.pdf |title=FRANCISCO J. AYALA doktorem honoris causa Uniwersytetu Warszawskiego Uroczystość wręczenia dyplomu |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref>

His scientific contributions in hydrobiology have been recognized by scientists who discovered a new genus of [[diatoms]] and named it ''Gliwiczia'' in his honour.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pth.home.pl/pobierz/Wiadomosci_3_2013.pdf |title=Wiadomości Hydrobiologiczne |access-date=5 July 2019}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286314699 |title=Gliwiczia gen. nov. a new monoraphid diatom genus from Lake Baikal with a description of four species new for science |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://diatoms.org/species/gliwiczia_calcar |title=Gliwiczia calcar |access-date=6 July 2019}}</ref>

Gliwicz died on 2 June 2024, at the age of 85.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wspomnienie o prof. Zbigniewie Macieju Gliwiczu |url=https://www.biol.uw.edu.pl/9118-2/ |website=biol.uw.edu.pl |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>
